scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The Connection Lab
scenes.caption: The Connection Lab asks a fictional text helper to explain a classroom water-filter demonstration. Its paragraph sounds confident and includes an impressive-looking reference. Tara opens the teacher’s source card before adding the paragraph to the project guide. Fluency alone cannot verify what the helper says.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: What changed?
scenes.caption: The source card records that visible particles were removed in the demonstration. It does not establish that the water is safe to drink, and the quoted reference is absent. Neel separates the observed result from the unsupported claim instead of copying both into a polished answer.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Follow the evidence
scenes.caption: The class uses only this supplied fictional text and does not test drinking water. Tara rewrites the explanation from checked evidence, marks the limitation and acknowledges the helper’s role. Private learner details are unnecessary in the request, and the learner remains responsible for the submitted explanation.
